title: Grateful Dead Live at Green Lake Aqua Theater on 1969-08-21
lineage: SBD > MC > C > D > CD > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: Soundboard recording captures a relaxed, psychedelic 1969 show with crisp guitars and standout performances of Morning Dew, Easy Wind, and an extended Other One/ Dark Star sequence.
ai_review.review: The Bear‑engineered soundboard tape is clear enough to hear the subtle bells, whistles, and the lush flute that colors this late‑summer Seattle gig.  The band rolls out a mellow setlist—early Casey Jones, the first-ever Easy Wind, a rare Minglewood, and a concise Dark Star—all delivered with relaxed vocals and smooth drumming, making it an appealing snapshot of the post‑Woodstock era.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers praise both the musical performance and the soundboard quality; only minor tape hiss is noted, yielding a strong overall rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp guitar and vocal presence, balanced mix; occasional slight tape hiss but overall clear and well‑balanced capture of stage ambience.

standout_songs: The That's It for the Other One > Dark Star > Cosmic Charlie
show_quality.setlist_flow: A laid‑back, meandering flow that moves from early Workingmen's classics into country‑flavored numbers and a relaxed jam sequence, showcasing the band's post‑Woodstock experimentation.

band_member_comments.Jerry: His voice is noted as beautiful and well‑served by the mix; vocal on Doin' That Rag praised.
band_member_comments.Keys: Flute addition (Charles Lloyd or Gary Larkey) adds a distinctive texture that works well with the band’s sound.
band_member_comments.Drums: Smooth, balanced drumming from Kreutzmann and Hart; rhythm described as relaxed and cohesive.
